To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a first order phase transition from the partonic to the hadronic phase is accompanied by a spinodal instability, which can lead to the formation of hadronic clusters, and by a dynamical instability which is a consequence of the expansion of the system.

the phase transition from quark gluon plasma to hadron matter is first order, the expansion of the quark-guon plasma in three dimensions leads to cluster formation, and the expansion of the plasma in one dimension leads to a new type of instabilities.
the parton plasma is dynamically unstable in the presence of a strong effective confinement, which is the reason why it decays into hadrons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the stability of the quark-guon plasma and the phase transition to hadrons.
the study of instabilities of the quark-guon plasma.
a better understanding of the dynamics of phase transitions and instabilities in relativistic heavy ion collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the parton plasma is unstable in the sense of thermodynamics and of linear response analysis.
the plasma is stable at equilibrium and unstable in the expansion.
the phase transition to hadrons is unstable and that the plasma is not able to reach thermal equilibrium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the parton plasma is unstable against a phase transition from the parton to the hadron phase, and that the instability is related to the formation of clusters.
the plasma expands into a hadron gas in a metastable state.
a first order phase transition from a parton plasma to hadron matter is not possible in the framework of quasi-particle models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the plasma is unstable to cluster formation.
the dynamical instabilities are not a consequence of a first-order phase-transition but are a consequence of the effective mass.
the plasma is unstable to cluster formation at a critical temperature which is about the same as the critical temperature at which the phase transition from parton to hadrons takes place.
